_readme: The DECLARED permissions of every GitHub App on the organisation. GitHub has no API to SET an
App's permissions, so this file can be verified against the live App but never applied:
scripts/github-app.sh <slug> verify. Change flow: PR this file first (a 'why' per permission;
a permission without a consumer is blast radius), then click it in the App settings and approve
the update on the installation, then verify. 'absent' = decided non-grants: a live grant of one
is drift, like a missing declared one.

apps.purpose: The agents' git identity: test-government-agents[bot] pushes branches and is the PR author, so a person can approve. Short-lived installation tokens, minted on the maintainer's machine.
apps.installs: selected repositories: the mock repositories, never .github

contents.why: clone and push branches (the rulesets keep it off default branches and tags)

issues.why: the maintenance queue: comment on and close the issues the scheduled checks open

actions.why: read workflow runs and logs of its own pushes

checks.why: read check results on a PR (fine-grained PATs cannot; App-only)

statuses.why: read commit statuses on a PR

absent.workflows: a branch workflow can ask for packages:write, so this is publish rights; workflow changes are pushed by a person
absent.administration: never: rulesets and repository settings are tofu/github, applied by an owner
absent.packages: publishing happens in GitHub Actions with the workflow's own GITHUB_TOKEN
